title: Simulated responses from large language models are weak proxies for human economic preferences across 74 countries
title_zh: 大型语言模型模拟的回答在74个国家中对人类经济偏好是弱代理
abstract: Large-scale surveys are central to investigating economic preferences but are costly and slow. Can large language model (LLM)-simulated responses substitute for human survey data? We conducted a virtual Global Preference Survey, simulating six experimentally validated economic preferences for 67,201 matched human respondents across 74 countries. Across 20 LLM configurations with diverse prompts and robustness checks, we found systematic but modest individual-level alignment (87.5% of Spearman correlations have 95% confidence intervals (CIs) above zero), with LLMs recovering the direction of associations in 77.8% (95% CI, (71.6%, 83.1%); CI-based consistency ratio) of gender, age and cognitive-ability dimensions, but only 48.1% (95% CI, (45.1%, 51.2%)) of cultural dimensions. Ablation and error decompositions suggest weaker alignment when removing demographic information than when removing country labels, and in many models alignment is weaker in economically undeveloped and less digitally connected countries. LLM-simulated responses may recover some individual- and group-level patterns but are not yet reliable proxies for cross-national representative surveys in macro-level inference or policy evaluation. Simulating a global survey of economic preferences across 74 countries, this study shows that large language models reproduce some demographic patterns in human preferences but fail to capture cultural differences, especially in lower-income countries.
abstract_zh: 大规模调查是研究经济偏好的核心，但成本高昂且耗时。大型语言模型（LLM）模拟的回答能否替代人类调查数据？我们进行了一项虚拟全球偏好调查，模拟了针对74个国家中67,201名匹配人类受试者的六种经证实的经济偏好。在20种不同提示和健壮性检查的LLM配置中，我们发现个体层面存在系统但适度的一致性（87.5%的斯皮尔曼相关系数95%置信区间（CI）高于零），LLMs在性别、年龄和认知能力维度上成功恢关联方向的比例为77.8%（95% CI，(71.6%，83.1%)；CI一致性比例），但在文化维度上仅为48.1%（95% CI，(45.1%，51.2%)）。消融和错误分解表明，去除人口统计信息后的对齐效果弱于去除国家标签，且在许多模型中，在经济落后和数字连接性较差的国家中，对齐效果更弱。LLM模拟的回答可能恢复个体和群体层面的某些模式，但目前尚不能作为跨国代表性调查在宏观推断或政策评估中的可靠代理。该研究通过模拟74个国家的全球经济偏好调查，表明大型语言模型能够再现人类偏好的某些人口统计模式，但未能捕捉到文化差异，特别是在低收入国家。
